subject: platform/perf
professional: a senior web performance engineer (owns JS budgets and code-splitting for a large site); first checks: does the import-graph walker see every edge the browser sees (minified imports, re-exports, src entry scripts, query strings), are byte counts what the wire carries, does 'exclusive' mean what a dominator/bundle analyzer would say, does it fail loudly when it cannot see a graph, and are the published numbers reproducible

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with an independent walker that uses V8's own ES module parser (vm.SourceTextModule.dependencySpecifiers, scratch /tmp/claude-0/round94-perf/indep.mjs) instead of the tools' regexes. module-weight.mjs sweep: 1,398 of the 1,400 pages the parser finds a module graph on agree to the byte and file count; 2 (medical-courier-route-margin, pool-route-pricing) are missed entirely because their minified inline `import{...}from'./calc.mjs'` has no whitespace the regex requires (`import\s+`, `\s+from`). Over-200 kB count 6 = 6. module-exclusive.mjs: on the pre-change ai-bookkeeper tree (git archive 88031b4cb^) receipts 47,413 B (46k), payouts 17,331 (17k), annualized 9,511 (9k) exactly as the parser walk; total 406,176 B = 397 KiB, 53 files. Gzip cross-checked against GNU gzip -6 -n (a separate deflate implementation): within 0.7% per file. But module-exclusive.mjs only reads inline `<script type="module">` bodies: on shed-designer (the write-up's next target, `<script type="module" src="app.mjs">`) it prints `total 0 kB gz 0 files` and exit 0, while the parser walk gives 393,127 B / 55 files; across all 1,406 venture pages the old tool printed zero for 19 and crashed on 1, with only 6 truly graph-less. Right where it sees the graph, silently wrong where it does not: 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed in the headers and docs/history/ai-bookkeeper-page-perf-2026-11-22.md: (1) sweep every ventures/*/index.html static graph, gzip total, largest first: works (1.8-2.1 s), misses 2 minified pages; (2) 'over 200 kB' count: works; (3) per-direct-import exclusive bytes 'for one page': works only for pages whose roots are inline imports, not for `src=` entry scripts (12 venture pages use one, shed-designer included) nor `?v=` import queries (readFileSync would throw); (4) the history doc's step 'run module-exclusive.mjs on it first' for shed-designer cannot be done with the tool as shipped. No README for platform/perf; the post points readers at the directory.
evidence.verification: No tests of any kind for either script, and no workflow triggers on platform/perf/** (grep .github/workflows: none). Seeded with quality_mutate.py against the only available check (a smoke run of each script): threshold 200*1024 -> 2000*1024 survived, exclusive set inverted (!rest.has -> rest.has) survived. Score 0: nothing would catch a bug. After this audit's fix, platform/perf/perf.test.mjs (5 tests, `node --test platform/perf/perf.test.mjs` 5 pass) catches 4/4 seeded mutants, and 3 of its 5 tests fail on the pre-fix scripts; the score records the state before the fix.
evidence.craft: Read both files whole (16 and 32 lines). Dependency-free and fast, but: dense one-line code (module-exclusive.mjs is 16 lines of statements joined by semicolons); the import regex is duplicated across the two files with drift (module-weight handles src= entries and strips ?query, module-exclusive does neither); regex scanning instead of a lexer (es-module-lexer, or vm.SourceTextModule as used here) so imports in strings/comments would count and minified/`export * as` forms do not; silent fallbacks: module-weight skips missing files and root-absolute `/x.mjs` imports (resolved against the filesystem root) without a word, module-exclusive reports 0 kB for a page it cannot read; 'kB' is KiB (/1024) unlabelled.
evidence.claims: Checked against recomputation: post/history '397 kB across 53 files' pass (406,176 B); '72 kB' pass (74,255 B = 72.5 KiB); '48 modules instead of 53 and 225 kB less raw JavaScript' pass (static graph raw bytes 1,160,293 -> 934,978, exactly the run record's Playwright numbers); 'six load more than 200 kB' pass; table rows shed 384, league 258, babysitting 240, wall-framing 238, xer 224 pass on the parent tree (xer 229,074 B); 'about a third of a second' pass (74,255*8/1.6 Mbit = 0.37 s); '1,398 pages load ES modules' partial (1,400; the tool's own blind spot). The module-exclusive header's promise for 'one page' and the doc's next-step advice for shed-designer fail (0 kB). Threshold ~200 kB is uncited.
evidence.fitness: The job: find which pages ship too much JS and which imports to defer. The sweep does the first well enough to have driven a real 72 kB saving on ai-bookkeeper. The second fails exactly where the next run needs it: the tool gives no answer on src-entry pages, and even after the fix it attributes bytes only to the page's direct imports, so for a single-entry app (shed-designer: one root, 384k, 'app.mjs' owns all) it cannot say which deeper import to split; a dominator-tree view is what that job needs.
evidence.domain: Compared with what a senior perf engineer would use (es-module-lexer or bundler metafile parsing, webpack-bundle-analyzer / source-map-explorer dominator attribution, Chrome DevTools Coverage, and brotli sizes, which is what Cloudflare usually serves for JS). Per-file gzip-6 is a reasonable proxy and the 'exclusive = not reachable from the other roots' definition is right for direct imports, but: no dominator analysis below the roots, no parse/compile cost, no brotli, regex not lexer. A sound first approximation, not a method a practitioner would sign off as is.

defects.what: module-exclusive.mjs reads only inline <script type="module"> bodies: a page whose entry is <script type="module" src=...> (shed-designer, the write-up's next target, and 12+ others) prints 'total 0 kB gz 0 files' with exit 0, a wrong number a perf run would act on; 19 of 1,406 pages printed zero and 1 crashed

Both import regexes require whitespace (import\s+, \s+from), so minified `import{a}from'./a.mjs'` is not an edge and `export * as ns from` is not matched: 2 of 1,400 pages (medical-courier-route-margin, pool-route-pricing) vanish from the sweep, and the post's 1,398 count is off by 2
No tests and no CI trigger for platform/perf: both seeded mutants (threshold, inverted exclusive set) survived
module-exclusive.mjs does not strip ?query/#hash from specifiers (module-weight does) and throws ENOENT on a missing file instead of reporting it

'Exclusive' is computed only for the page's direct imports; there is no dominator-tree attribution below the roots, so for a single-entry app (shed-designer: one root owns all 384 kB) the tool cannot say which deeper import to make dynamic

Regex scanning instead of a lexer: an import-shaped line inside a template string or comment counts as an edge (missing targets are skipped silently in module-weight); root-absolute '/x.mjs' specifiers resolve against the filesystem root and are dropped without a warning
Sizes are gzip -6 per file and labelled kB but computed as KiB; Cloudflare typically serves brotli for JS, and parse/compile cost is not measured; the ~200 kB threshold is uncited
No README for platform/perf; the post sends readers to the directory, and the regex is duplicated across the two scripts with drift (src= and ?query handled in one only)

verdict: platform/perf is two small, fast, dependency-free scripts that did real work: every number the 2026-11-22 ai-bookkeeper write-up and post cite (397 kB / 53 files, 46+17+9 kB exclusive, 53 -> 48 modules, 1,160,293 -> 934,978 raw bytes, six pages over 200 kB) reproduces against a walker built on V8's own module parser and against GNU gzip. But module-exclusive.mjs silently reports 0 kB for any page whose entry is a <script type=module src> tag, including shed-designer, the very page the write-up tells the next run to examine with it, and both regexes miss minified imports (2 of 1,400 pages). There were no tests and no CI trigger; both seeded mutants survived. A senior web performance engineer would want a lexer, dominator attribution below the page's roots, and brotli sizes. Correctness 2, verification 0: below the bar. This audit fixed defects 0, 1 and 3 in platform/perf (src= roots, ?query stripping, minified and `export * as` forms, a loud exit 1 when no graph is found) and added platform/perf/perf.test.mjs (5 tests; 3 fail on the pre-fix code; 4/4 seeded mutants caught); after the fix both scripts agree with the parser walk on all 1,400 pages. Scores are before the fix.
